page: Amazon Web Services r5dn.24xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 96 vCPUs and 48 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL processor operating at 3.1 GHz. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical core. Local storage is bundled, consisting of 3600 GB of NVMe SSD space, and the instance delivers a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core and memory performance. The instance achieves a strong rating in stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and passmark CPU score. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 4502.68 GB/sec and large block uncached speeds at 215.93 GB/sec. However, single-core performance represents a notable tradeoff, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance and gzip compression single-threaded both scoring in the weak category.

Given its high memory density, bundled NVMe storage, and 100 Gbps network baseline, the r5dn.24xlarge is designed for memory-intensive and network-bound workloads. It demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, as evidenced by 75.03 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a strong static web serving throughput of 44.7 GB/sec. Conversely, it is poorly suited for LLM text generation, where it registers poor to weak speeds. The instance offers high resource density for large-scale databases, caching layers, and memory-intensive data processing pipelines.
